## Issues/Devitaions/Comments
This assumes lazy labelling of the si_mucosa where "marginal" etc is used instead of "marginal_orientation".
```{r}
library(readxl)
library(jsonlite)
library(tidyverse)
library(caret)


validate_si_mucosa <- function(reviewed) {
 reviewed <- reviewed %>%
   mutate(target = case_when(
     ((classification == "marginal_orientation" & is.na(correction)) | correction == "marginal") ~ "marginal_orientation",
     ((classification == "inadequate_orientation" & is.na(correction)) | correction == "inadequate") ~ "inadequate_orientation",
     ((classification == "adequate_orientation" & is.na(correction)) | correction == "adequate") ~ "adequate_orientation",
     ((classification == "no_si_mucosa" & is.na(correction)) | correction == "no_si") ~ "no_si_mucosa",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ))
 
 # Factor levels (ensure consistent order)
  orientation_levels <- c("adequate_orientation", "marginal_orientation", 
                          "inadequate_orientation", "no_si_mucosa")
  
  # Confusion matrix
  conf_matrix <- confusionMatrix(
    factor(reviewed$classification, levels = orientation_levels),
    factor(reviewed$target, levels = orientation_levels)
  )
  
  # Prepare data for plot
  cm_df <- as.data.frame(conf_matrix$table)
  colnames(cm_df) <- c("Predicted", "Actual", "Freq")
  
  # Confusion matrix heatmap
  confusion_matrix <- ggplot(cm_df, aes(x = Actual, y = Predicted, fill = Freq)) +
    geom_tile(color = "black") +
    geom_text(aes(label = Freq), size = 4, family = "Arial") +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "orange") +
    scale_x_discrete(position = "top") +
    scale_y_discrete(limits = rev(orientation_levels)) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 0),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 9, family = "Arial"),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 9, family = "Arial"),
      axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
      legend.position = "right"
    ) +
    labs(x = "Actual Class", y = "Predicted Class",
         fill = "Count")

  # Performance metrics table
  by_class <- as.data.frame(conf_matrix$byClass)

  if (is.null(rownames(by_class))) {
    rownames(by_class) <- orientation_levels[1]  # binary case
  } else {
    rownames(by_class) <- orientation_levels
  }

  performance_metrics <- by_class %>%
    rename(prevalence = Prevalence,
           se = Sensitivity,
           sp = Specificity,
           ppv = `Pos Pred Value`,
           npv = `Neg Pred Value`,
           f1 = F1,
           balanced_accuracy = `Balanced Accuracy`) %>%
    select(prevalence, se, sp, ppv, npv, f1, balanced_accuracy)

  return(list(confusion_matrix = confusion_matrix,
              performance_metrics = performance_metrics))
}
```

### Validate si_mucosa on labl_2020_tuning
#### Issues/Deviations/Comments
This set was used for setting parameters - basically training performance (although not as big risk of
overfitting as an ML model)
```{r}
reviewed <- read_xlsx("~/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/Projects/fe_si_models/si_mucosa/input/reviewed_si_mucosa_labl_2020_tuning.xlsx")

output_dir <- "~/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/Projects/fe_si_models/si_mucosa/output/validate_si_mucosa/"
validated <- validate_si_mucosa(reviewed)

print(validated$confusion_matrix)
print(validated$performance_metrics)

png(paste0(output_dir, "confusion_matrix_si_mucosa_labl_2020_tuning.png"), width = 7, height = 3, units = "in", res = 300)
plot(validated$confusion_matrix)  # Replace with your actual plotting function if needed
dev.off()

write_json(validated$performance_metrics, paste0(output_dir, "performance_si_mucosa_labl_2020_tuning.json"), pretty = TRUE)
```
